name: Cafe Renaissance
note: Persian and Mediterranean cafe whose owner bought the former Plantation restaurant here in 1991 and turned it toward Persian food, as a 1998 Palo Alto Weekly review described. A downtown lunch spot into the 2010s, it was later replaced by Curry Up Now; its exact closing year is not confirmed.

name: Campo 185
note: Farm-to-table Italian restaurant, also called Campo Pizzeria, that opened in December 2012 in the former Lavanda space at University and Emerson. It closed in 2013 after about nine months, and its owners then opened Sam's Chowder House in the space.

name: John's Cafe
note: Panini and coffee cafe that took over the former Lytton Roasting Company corner in 2012; it closed in January 2015 after three years.

name: Selix Formal Wear
note: Tuxedo and formal wear shop, a few doors from its 1959–1963 location at 158 University Ave. It closed in February 2015 when the Selix chain went bankrupt and shut all six stores; when it moved here is unknown.

name: Coupa Cafe
note: Venezuelan-style cafe in the Lytton Gateway building across from the downtown Caltrain station, opened in late January 2016 as Coupa's second downtown Palo Alto location. The family's original cafe opened on Ramona Street in 2004.

name: Ike's Love & Sandwiches
note: Bay Area sandwich chain. Its owner took over the former John's Cafe lease in 2015, but city approvals delayed the opening until November 27, 2018.

name: Indian Bowl
note: Bowling alley, described as Palo Alto's longest-lasting, in a 1926 building that runs through to 734 Ramona St, entered from Emerson Street. It opened in the early 1940s after a 1940 remodel and closed in 1975, when Baker Graphics took over the space.

name: Bijou Theatre
note: Single-screen movie theater with about 300 seats that opened August 12, 1964 with Dr. Strangelove and closed in the late 1980s. Gordon Biersch opened in the former theater building in 1988.

name: The Gatehouse
note: Restaurant in the former Tinney & Sons mortuary building, remodeled for it in 1974. It ran about 20 years until Jeremiah Tower bought the site for Stars in 1994.

name: Baker Graphics
note: Commercial printing firm that moved into the former Indian Bowl bowling alley after it closed in 1975, later expanding through the building from Emerson St to Ramona St. It is recorded in the city's historic buildings inventory, revised in 1985.

name: Cardinal Barber Shop
note: Traditional barbershop in the Cardinal Hotel building, reached through the hotel lobby and part of the building since about 1925. Its current barber has worked there since 1982.

name: Palo Alto Speedometer
note: Repair and restoration shop for car speedometers, tachometers, gauges and clocks, still open today. The business says it has been on Emerson Street since 1957.

name: President Barber Shop
note: Long-running barbershop in the Hotel President building, still open today. A 2004 Palo Alto Weekly profile traced its University Avenue roots to the late 1920s, and one co-owner ran it from 1960 to 2004.

name: Sam's Barber Styling Shop
note: Neighborhood barbershop on the 400 block of Lytton Ave near Cowper St, opened by barber Sam Sanchez on July 13, 1967. It was still operating at the same address decades later.

name: Union Bank
note: Bank branch, earlier the main office of The Stanford Bank (founded 1964), which merged into Union Bank in 1971. Later known as MUFG Union Bank, it became a U.S. Bank branch in 2023 after U.S. Bancorp bought Union Bank.

name: Palo Alto Bicycles
note: Family-owned bike shop that grew out of the Palo Alto Sport Shop's bicycle department and was renamed Palo Alto Bicycles when it moved here in 1973. It briefly operated across the street at 170 University in 1997–98 while this building was seismically rebuilt.

name: Bank of America
note: Bank branch in a building put up for Bank of America around 1974. The bank moved here in 1976 from 251 University Ave, where its predecessor, First National Bank, had merged with the Bank of Italy in 1928.

name: Arnoldi Jewelers
note: Family-owned fine jewelry store started by a goldsmith from Italy who came to the Bay Area in 1978, the year the business gives as its founding. It is open today at this address; how long it has been here is not confirmed.

name: Letter Perfect
note: Fine stationery and gift shop, open today. Business listings say it has been independently owned and operated since 1982; it may not have been at this address the whole time.

name: Palo Alto Eyes
note: Optometry practice and optical shop that has served Palo Alto since 1983, though it's not documented when it first opened at this address. It moved to 220 Hamilton Ave in 2026.

name: The Cowper Inn
note: Bed and breakfast in two restored 1890s houses at 705 and 711 Cowper St, at Forest Ave, opened around 1986 and still operating. The same owners ran it for about 20 years and put it up for sale in 2006.

name: Garden Court Hotel
note: 62-room Spanish-style boutique hotel that opened in 1986 on the former site of the Cowper Court Apartments. After 35 years as the Garden Court, it was renamed el Prado Hotel in 2021.

name: Whole Foods Market
note: Natural foods supermarket that opened in 1989 in a remodeled existing building. It was the chain's first store on the West Coast and is still open.

name: NY Pizza
note: Small New York-style pizzeria selling slices and whole pies, open since about 1990. A 2003 Palo Alto Weekly review described the shop as barely 15 feet wide, and it is still open at the same address.

name: De Novo Fine Contemporary Jewelry
note: Contemporary art jewelry gallery that opened in November 1990, with its entrance on Ramona St just off University Ave. It is still open today.

name: Rose and Crown
note: British pub that earlier ran under other tavern names and took the name The Rose & Crown in 1990; its painted trompe l'oeil facade dates to 1991. Still open.

name: Peet's Coffee
note: Peet's cafe on Homer Avenue next to Whole Foods, opened in 1992. It closed briefly in early 2026, then reopened in April 2026 after a lease extension.

name: Charmelle 28
note: Fine lingerie boutique that opened downtown in late 1993 as Gitti's Fine Lingerie and later took the name Charmelle 28. It was absorbed by Lingerie République around 2019.

name: Duxiana
note: Bed showroom, open today. State home-furnishings license records place it at 534 Bryant St from 1993.

name: Richard Sumner Frames and Prints
note: Custom frame shop and print gallery, listed in the Palo Alto Weekly in January 1994 and still open. In 2021 the Weekly described it as having served downtown for more than 30 years, so it may have opened before 1994.

name: Stapleton Florist
note: Florist in a narrow pink building on Waverley Street, named Palo Alto's best florist in the Palo Alto Weekly's Best of 1994. It may be older, and the shop at this address and phone number is now also listed as Michaela's Flower Shop.

name: Wells Fargo
note: Bank branch, still open today. It was open by the mid-1990s and took in customers from First Interstate's closing 525 University Ave branch in 1996; it may be older.

name: Darbar Indian Cuisine
note: Indian restaurant serving north and south Indian dishes, with a weekday lunch buffet. A 2007 review says the owner opened his Palo Alto storefront in 1995, and it was at this address by 2007; still open today.

name: Tea Time
note: Tea room serving afternoon tea and loose-leaf teas, still open today. A tea directory lists it as established in 1995, and it changed hands in early 2006.

name: Nola's
note: New Orleans-themed restaurant and bar in a Spanish-style courtyard building on Ramona Street, open since June 1996 and still operating.

name: Fidelity Investments
note: Fidelity investor center, open today. Fidelity fund reports filed with the SEC listed this walk-in office by mid-1996, and it may be older.

name: Elite Cleaners and Tailors
note: Dry cleaner in the 460-468 University Ave building, a tenant there by 1997 that returned after that year's renovation and is still open. A dry cleaner with the same name was listed at 464 University Ave from 1944 to 1963 and may be the same business.

name: Bryant Street Gallery
note: Art gallery and frame shop, still open. It celebrated its 25th anniversary in 2025, so it opened around 2000.

name: Bridge Bank
note: Bank branch on the ground floor of the Palo Alto Office Center at University Ave and Cowper St; the bank leased the space from late 2001 and opened around 2002. Bridge Bank became part of Western Alliance Bank in 2015.

name: Wells Fargo
note: Bank branch, still open today. Federal banking records list this branch as established in July 2002.

name: Old Pro
note: Sports bar, the downtown branch of a Palo Alto bar that started on El Camino Real in 1964. It opened on Ramona Street around 2003, became the main location after the El Camino bar closed in 2007, and closed in June 2022.

name: Skin Spirit
note: Medical spa (facials, injectables and laser treatments) founded in downtown Palo Alto in 2003, with its flagship clinic at 701 Emerson St. It is still open and has grown into a multi-state chain.

name: Buca di Beppo
note: Italian chain restaurant, open on Emerson Street by early 2003 and still open today; it may have opened around 2002.

name: Chico's
note: Women's clothing store, open today. A 2004 charity auction offered a shopping party at this store, so it was open by then; the exact opening year is unknown.

name: Tai Pan
note: Hong Kong-style Cantonese restaurant, open since about 2005 according to business listings and a 2006 local review. Still open in 2026.

name: Romi Boutique
note: Women's clothing boutique, open today. The boutique says it was founded in 2005; it has been listed at this address since at least 2013.

name: Bistro Maxine
note: French crepe cafe serving sweet and savory crepes, salads and sandwiches. Palo Alto Online reported it opening in June 2006, and it is still open.

name: Lee Optometrics
note: Family optometry office and eyewear shop, still open. The practice says it has been in downtown Palo Alto since 2006, and federal provider records list it at this address from January 2007.

name: The Wine Room
note: Wine bar that opened in November 2007 in the 1925 Pedro de Lemos building first used by the Gotham Shop, taking over the former BayLeaf Cafe space. Its sign is an updated version of the Gotham Shop's original design.

name: Yoga Source
note: Yoga studio, still open. Listed at this address in local yoga-studio guides from 2007 and 2009; the studio says it has been in Palo Alto about 30 years, so it may have been here earlier.

name: Pampas
note: Brazilian churrascaria, where waiters bring grilled meats on skewers to the table. It opened on April 29, 2008 in a remodeled building on Alma Street and was billed as the first churrasco-style restaurant in the South Bay.

name: Sprout
note: Build-your-own salad cafe that opened in late August 2008 in the former Windy's Chinese restaurant space. Still open today.

name: Avidbank
note: Local commercial bank, called The Private Bank of the Peninsula until 2011, with its main office here from December 2008. The office closed in fall 2017 when the headquarters moved to San Jose and the Palo Alto branch moved to 437 Lytton Ave.

name: Patagonia
note: Outdoor clothing and gear store, still open, in a brick building that housed auto dealerships in the 1920s–1950s. A local news column places it on Alma St by early 2008, and it may have opened earlier.

name: Coconuts Caribbean Restaurant & Bar
note: Jamaican restaurant and bar across from City Hall, opened in September 2008 by chef Robert Simpson of Back A Yard. It is known for jerk dishes and oxtail, with live steel-drum music on weekend evenings.

name: Starbucks
note: Starbucks at 374–376 University Ave, open here from about 2008 until April 30, 2023, when it moved to 151 University.

name: Scotty's
note: Neighborhood bar and grill opened in 2009 by a longtime Empire Tap Room bartender, in space formerly used by Maddalena's and Cafe Fino. Still open.

name: Reposado
note: Upscale Mexican restaurant that opened in early January 2009 in the former Caffe Verona space. It is still operating and opened a second location in San Mateo in 2026.

name: Garden Fresh Vegan
note: Vegan Chinese restaurant, a second branch of a Mountain View favorite, that opened on Ramona Street in spring 2010. It was reported permanently closed in 2023, while the Mountain View restaurant stayed open.

name: Parasol
note: Parasol Beauty Atelier is a skin care, brow and permanent makeup studio. Business listings say it opened around November 2010, and it is still open.

name: Hotel Keen
note: Boutique hotel that opened in May 2010 after a renovation of the former Palo Alto Hotel, a low-income residential hotel bought by new owners in 2008. Still open today.

name: Chase
note: Open today (bank). A photo shows Chase here by August 2010; the branch was a Washington Mutual in 2006 and probably became Chase after JPMorgan Chase took over that bank in 2008.

name: Philz Coffee
note: Philz Coffee cafe at Forest Avenue and Alma Street, announced in mid-2011 to open that September and open by early 2012. It still operates there.

name: Pizza My Heart
note: Slice shop from the Santa Cruz-area chain that took over the former Pizza A Go-Go spot on University Ave; members of local history groups remember it there by 2011, and it may be older. Still open at this address.

name: Oren's Hummus Shop
note: Israeli restaurant opened in 2011 by tech entrepreneur Oren Dobronsky and still open today. This was the first location of what became a small Bay Area chain.

name: The Core
note: Shoe store run by Footwear Etc., open today. It is documented here by April 2011, when it hosted MBT shoe events, and may be older.

name: Lytton Cleaners
note: Dry cleaner at 489 Lytton Ave, still open today. It has been on the map since at least 2013 and may be much older.

name: Starbucks
note: Starbucks at University & High, opened in 2023 in the former Lemonade space after moving from 376 University.

name: Empire Grill & Tap Room
note: Restaurant and bar that was a downtown fixture for about 21 years before closing in April 2013. Pizzeria Delfina later moved into the space.

name: Rangoon
note: Burmese and Chinese restaurant opened in 1992 by chef Mike Wong and his wife. Palo Alto Online described the site as Rangoon's former location by August 2012, so it had closed by then.

name: Kan Zeman
note: Mediterranean restaurant that opened around 2002 in the former Jim's Coffee Shop space. It closed in May 2011 after losing its lease, and its owners moved operations to their Med Wraps shop across the street.

name: Sushi Tomo
note: Sushi restaurant that opened in 2006, the same year as its sister location on El Camino Way. It closed in fall 2015 and Shoji Sushi took over the space that October.

name: Joya
note: Latin-inspired tapas restaurant and lounge that opened in August 2008. It closed after about 15 years, and Khazana later took over the space.

name: Mills the Florist
note: Florist on the corner of University Ave and Ramona St, one of a family business that began in 1903 as a nursery on Palo Alto Ave and had earlier shops elsewhere on University Ave. The year it moved to this corner is uncertain, and it is still listed as open.

name: St. Thomas Aquinas Church
note: Palo Alto's oldest surviving church building, a Carpenter Gothic Catholic church at Waverley and Homer that held its first Mass on June 4, 1902, and still holds services. It was the funeral location in the 1971 film Harold and Maude.

name: First Church of Christ, Scientist
note: Mission Revival church designed by Elmer Grey, built in 1916 and dedicated in 1917; it held services until the congregation merged in 2006. The city named it a historic structure in 1978, and the building was later turned into offices.

name: Reed Electric Co
note: Family-run electrical shop in the 1897 house at 621 High St, the Reed family's home and shop from about the 1930s. It was listed in city directories from 1939, and the city's historic buildings inventory notes it was still an electric company in 1985.

name: John F. Dahl Plumbing
note: Plumbing, heating and air conditioning shop, founded in 1895 on University Ave and later on Alma St. It was still there in 1995, its 100th year; directory listings since then appear under Palo Alto Plumbing and Dahl Plumbing.

name: McMillan Coffee Co
note: Coffee shop listed in Palo Alto city directories from 1946 to 1963. A 2013 obituary says a local owner ran the business downtown for 15 years from about 1980, so it likely lasted until about 1995.

name: Rita on Ramona
note: Specialty shop in the arcade building at 532-536 Ramona. It appears in city directories from 1951 to 1963 and was still listed as a tenant in the building's 1985 historic inventory.

name: Gleim the Jeweler
note: Family jewelry store, listed here in city directories from 1951, which had earlier been at other University Ave addresses. The downtown store closed in early summer 2009 when the business consolidated into its Stanford Shopping Center and Los Altos stores.

name: Eyerly's
note: Hardware and appliance store, listed at this address in city directories from 1954. It began on University Ave about 1947, later moved here, and closed in 1980, according to Palo Alto Online.

name: The Tangent
note: Pizza parlor and deli with an upstairs folk-music room, the Top of the Tangent, which opened in January 1963. It was still serving food and hosting live music in 1969; its closing date is unknown.

name: Il Fornaio
note: Italian restaurant in the Garden Court Hotel (renamed el PRADO Hotel in 2021), opened in 1989 according to the company's history. It served its last meal on January 18, 2026, when its lease ended, after about 36 years downtown.

name: Woman's Club of Palo Alto
note: Clubhouse of the Woman's Club of Palo Alto, a civic and philanthropic group founded in 1894. The Tudor-Craftsman building by Charles Edward Hodges opened in 1916 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

name: University AME Zion Church
note: Palo Alto's oldest Black church, founded in 1918, worshipped in this building from its dedication in 1925 until moving to Middlefield Road around 1965. The preserved building later became part of a commercial development.

name: City of Paris Dyeing and Cleaning Works
note: Dyeing and cleaning works in a Mission Revival building by Roy Heald, built about 1925-28. The firm began in 1922 on Ramona St and was run here until about 1985.

name: Palo Alto Police & Fire Station
note: Palo Alto's first combined police and fire station, a 1927 Birge Clark building. The police moved to the new City Hall around 1970, and the building later became the Avenidas senior center.

name: Barker Hotel
note: Residential hotel built in 1928 that came to house very low-income residents. The Palo Alto Housing Corporation (now Alta Housing) acquired it in 1994, and it still operates as affordable single-room-occupancy housing.

name: Ellison's Body Shop
note: Family-run auto body repair and towing shop founded May 1, 1929 by Earl Ellison Sr.; by 1995 it was one of only two body shops left downtown, and it ceased business in 2000. The building remains as a historical site.

name: Palo Alto Medical Clinic
note: Group medical practice in the Spanish Colonial Revival Roth Building, designed by Birge Clark in 1932. The clinic later moved out, and the city bought the building in 2000 to become the home of the Palo Alto History Museum.

name: Paddleford Oldsmobile
note: Oldsmobile-Cadillac dealership that George Paddleford bought in 1935 at Emerson and Homer and ran for more than 50 years. Its building was later remodeled for Whole Foods Market.

name: Peninsula Plating Works
note: Family-run plating shop at the back of a silversmith's store on Homer Ave, run by three generations of the same family. Founded about 1939 and still open in 1994; it is said to have closed around 2003.

name: Woolworth's
note: Woolworth's five-and-dime moved to this larger store at 352 University Ave in 1949 and remained a downtown fixture until it closed in 1989.

name: Lucky Store
note: Lucky supermarket, listed at this address in directories from 1950 through 1965; actual years open may be longer.

name: House of Foam
note: Downtown foam and upholstery shop at 150 Hamilton Ave. Owner Bob Tallman told the Weekly in 2014 that nothing in the shop had changed since the 1950s and that fittings on the wall dated from the 1950s under the original owner; Tallman bought the shop from a family friend in the 1970s and ran it virtually unchanged until it closed in the first week of January 2020. name: The Camera Shop
note: Downtown camera store that advertised in the 1961 Palo Alto High School yearbook. It is remembered as closing in the mid-1970s, and some of its staff later worked at Keeble & Shuchat; actual years open may be longer.

name: Gallery House
note: Artist-run cooperative gallery founded in 1958; after earlier locations it spent 38 years at 538 Ramona St. before moving to California Avenue in 2000.

name: Dana Morgan Music
note: Music shop selling and repairing instruments with teaching rooms in the back, where Jerry Garcia taught guitar and banjo in the early 1960s and met Bob Weir on New Year's Eve 1963. It was still operating in 1968, when it bought an advertising slot in the program for the Thelonious Monk concert at Palo Alto High School.

name: Stanford Electric Works
note: Lighting and electrical shop that had been in Palo Alto since about 1914 and at the corner of High St and Everett Ave from 1964. It moved to Mountain View in June 2013 after the property was sold to the owner of a dermatology chain.

name: Pacific Art League
note: Nonprofit art center with a gallery and classes in the 1926 Birge Clark building that once housed Winsor's cabinet shop. Founded in 1921 as the Palo Alto Art Club, it bought the building in 1965 and was renamed the Pacific Art League in 1984.

name: Wiedeman's
note: Men's fine clothing store that opened in Palo Alto in 1906; it moved to 281 University Ave at Bryant Street in 1965, tripled in size, and closed in early May 1995 after almost 89 years in business, as the city's fifth-oldest downtown business.

name: The Poppycock
note: Fish-and-chips restaurant with a music room at University and High, remembered as Palo Alto's first regular rock venue, booking folk, blues and rock acts from 1967 until about 1970. The space later became the jazz club In Your Ear, and the building burned down at the end of 1972.

name: Commuter Shell Service
note: Full-service Shell gas station on the corner of Alma St and Lytton Ave, run by the same operators for 42 years; downtown Palo Alto's only gas station, open around the clock, until Shell pulled out and it closed at the end of June 2010. The site later became the Lytton Gateway building.

name: Smith Andersen Gallery
note: Fine art gallery run by Paula Kirkeby, opened in October 1969 at 200 Homer St and later at 728 Emerson St. It closed Aug. 1, 1996.

name: Celia's
note: Mexican restaurant that served downtown Palo Alto for a quarter-century before closing in the last week of November 1994; All Seasons Chinese Restaurant then moved into its space at 423 University Ave.

name: Tallman's House of Foam
note: A longtime downtown foam shop that sold foam and made custom cases. Owner Bob Tallman took it over in the 1970s, and it quietly closed in early January 2020.

name: Palo Alto City Hall
note: Palo Alto's city hall, designed by Edward Durell Stone and finished around 1970 on the site of the 1904 Carnegie Library, which was torn down in 1967. The plaza in front was later named King Plaza, and the building is still the seat of city government.

name: Downtown Library
note: The Downtown Branch of the Palo Alto Public Library opened here on March 8, 1971, across from the new Civic Center. It replaced the Carnegie library, which was demolished in 1967. The branch was renovated in 2011 and is still open.

name: In Your Ear
note: Live music club at University and High that opened in May 1971 in the former Poppycock space, booking touring jazz, blues and rock acts. It closed on New Year's Eve 1972, when a fire started by the club's pizza oven destroyed the building.

name: Festival Cinema
note: A 114-seat revival movie house in a converted office building. It opened in October 1972 as the Academy Cinema, was later renamed the Festival Cinema, and closed in April 1985.

name: St. Michael's Alley
note: Revival of the 1959 University Avenue coffeehouse, opened in 1973 in the 1923 Cashel building at Emerson and Homer. The founding owner sold it in 1994.

name: United Nations Association Gift Shop
note: Volunteer-run gift shop selling UNICEF cards and fair-trade crafts from around the world, known locally as the UNICEF store. Created in 1974, it moved to its Emerson Street storefront just north of Hamilton Ave and is still operating there.

name: Chantilly
note: French and Northern Italian restaurant that opened in 1974 in the Gotham Shop courtyard building at 520 Ramona St; a 1980 photo shows its courtyard entrance there. Around 1989 it moved next door to 530 Ramona and became Chantilly II, which the map already lists separately.

name: Great American Framing Company
note: Custom picture-framing shop founded in 1974 that was for years in the former dining room of the Cardinal Hotel. It later moved to El Camino Real in Barron Park, outside downtown; the year it moved is approximate.

name: Ranch Room Pizza
note: Pizza parlor named as the occupant of this small 1929 Early California-style building in the October 1975 Santa Clara County heritage inventory. The years it was open are not known beyond that listing.

name: Good Earth Restaurant and Bakery
note: Health-food restaurant and bakery from a national chain. It opened in March 1976 in the former House of Pies building and closed in 2001 when the owner retired.

name: Maddalena's
note: Elegant white-tablecloth Continental restaurant at 544 Emerson St. Fred Maddalena took over the former Golden Dragon space in 1976 and ran it for 31 years; it served its last meal on May 19, 2007 after the landlord did not renew the lease.

name: Jim's Coffee Shop
note: Downtown breakfast diner, run for about 24 years by Barney Kang and known for the doughnuts in its window, that was a gathering spot for city officials, police and reporters. When Kang retired in March 2000 it was called Palo Alto's last diner, and the space later became Kan Zeman.

name: Avenidas
note: Senior services center in the city-owned 1927 Birge Clark former police and fire station, opened around 1977–78 by the Senior Coordinating Council, which later took the name Avenidas. The building was renovated and expanded, reopening in 2019.

name: Ramona's Pizza
note: Long-running downtown pizzeria and Stanford-student gathering spot; the owner bought it in 1978 and it closed in 2003, after which the Old Pro took over the space.

name: St. Michael's Waiting Room
note: Small venue next door to St. Michael's Alley that held weekly poetry readings and open-mic nights, in the spirit of the original 1959 coffeehouse. It closed around the time the restaurant was sold in 1994; its opening year is uncertain.

name: Palo Alto Bimmer
note: Independent BMW and MINI auto repair shop that opened in January 1980 at the 1929 gas station premises on Alma Street and still operates there; reviews and city permits place it at 799 Alma St. through the 2000s.

name: Stanford Bookstore
note: Downtown branch of the Stanford Bookstore at the corner of University and High, specializing in medical and technical books. It opened in 1981 and closed June 30, 2007, when the store moved into the main campus bookstore at White Plaza.

name: Reach Fitness Club
note: Downtown gym that opened in Palo Alto in 1982 and ran its fitness center at 707 High St. (listed there in the 1994 Best of) for 36 years, closing Dec. 15, 2018; its Pilates studio at 833 Emerson St. stayed open.

name: Chimera Books and Music
note: Used bookstore in an 1897 house, listed at this address in 1982. Around 1990 it moved to University Avenue, and in 1999 it left for Redwood City.

name: The Photographer's Gallery
note: Fine art photography gallery at 732 Emerson St for 13 years; owner Amy Saret moved it to 536 Ramona St on Aug. 1, 1995, and the women's clothing store Virtuelle took over the Emerson space that October.

name: Caffe Verona
note: Beloved downtown coffeehouse and Italian cafe that moved to 236 Hamilton Ave in 1984 and closed August 31, 2003 after 19 years, when its landlord declined to renew the lease. It was a famous meeting spot for entrepreneurs and neighborhood regulars.

name: Theo's
note: Seafood restaurant, a Palo Alto institution for 11 years and possibly the city's first pink, chrome and cane-back-chair restaurant; owner Michael Aroner closed it in October 1995 and reopened the space as the Mystic Cafe.

name: Watercourse Way
note: Bathhouse day spa with private hot tub rooms, in the 1931 former French laundry building at High St and Channing Ave, which was remodeled for it in 1984. The business says it opened in Palo Alto in 1980, and it is still open.

name: The Victorian on Lytton
note: Bed-and-breakfast inn in the 1896 Queen Anne-style Hannah Clapp House, which was converted to an inn in 1985–86. It closed around 2006 after water damage, and the house later held a women's resource center.

name: Douglas Fabrics
note: A Palo Alto Stanford Heritage photo dated around 1986 shows Douglas Fabrics at 355 University Ave; that dated photo is the only sighting, so both years are 1986.

name: Stanford Pub and Grill
note: Pub and grill on Emerson Street, also called the Stanford Pub, run by its founding owner for about eight years. It had closed by September 1994, and Left at Albuquerque later opened in the space.

name: Fran's Market
note: Longtime neighborhood market at Lytton and Gilman; the space became Mademoiselle Colette bakery in 2016–17. Opening year unknown; Fran's Smoke Shop was listed next door at 497 Lytton in the 1950s. Palo Alto Online's Peninsula Foodist reported it closing in 2017.

name: Miyake
note: Noisy, flashy sushi restaurant in the historic Fraternal Hall building, famous for sake bombs and a loud, crowded bar scene. It ran for about 25 years before closing in September 2012.

name: Cafe Fino
note: Fred Maddalena's smaller art-deco nightclub next door to Maddalena's restaurant, sharing its kitchen and menu with live jazz, cabaret acts and tango lessons; it opened in 1989 and closed shortly after Maddalena's shut in May 2007.

name: Mandarin Gourmet
note: Chinese restaurant that was at this address for many years, until about 2014. Bird Dog opened in the space in late 2015. Palo Alto Online's Peninsula Foodist reported it closing in 2015.

name: Chantilly II
note: French and Northern Italian restaurant with a courtyard setting that opened on Ramona Street as Chantilly in 1974 and was called Chantilly II from about 1990. It was popular with tech-industry diners and moved to Redwood City in 1999.

name: Diddams Amazing Party Store
note: Party and toy store, part of a local Peninsula chain. Palo Alto Online reported it was due to close in March 2010, about 20 years after it opened.

name: Palermo Ristorante
note: Small, family-owned Italian restaurant and a longtime University Avenue favorite, remembered open by 1991 (it may be older). It moved out in 2005; the space later became Chicken Ranch, Mint Leaf, Han Fine Korean Cuisine and Umami Burger.

name: Blue Chalk Cafe
note: Southern restaurant and bar across from City Hall, with blue felt pool tables and shuffleboard. It opened around 1992 and closed in early 2010.

name: La Pastaia Ristorante Italiano
note: Italian restaurant known for its duck-and-ricotta spinach ravioli. The Palo Alto Weekly reviewed it in 1993 and still listed it in 1994, and Evvia later took over the space.

name: Nouveau Trattoria
note: Franco-Italian trattoria run by chef-owner Annie Nunan, a reincarnation of the old Trattoria Romana, with live jazz nightly and family-style Basque dinners; reviewed in April 1993 and still going in 1999, it was renamed Annie's in 2003.

name: Bangkok Cuisine
note: Small Thai restaurant on Lytton Avenue, reviewed by the Palo Alto Weekly in December 1993. It was still in the Weekly's restaurant listings in May 2001, and its actual opening and closing years may differ.

name: La Morenita
note: Family-run Mexican restaurant at Emerson and Homer that opened in May 1994 and closed in December 2017 when the owners retired. The Greek restaurant Taverna later took over the space. Palo Alto Online's Peninsula Foodist reported it opening in 1994 and closing in 2017.

name: St. Michael's Alley
note: California bistro run by the owners who bought St. Michael's Alley in 1994, in the space next door to the 800 Emerson original. The restaurant later moved to Homer Avenue, and the Emerson space served as its Annex until Taverna took it over around 2019.

name: Q Cafe & Billiards
note: Restaurant, nightclub and pool hall in a warehouse-style building on Alma Street, with billiards, live music and DJ nights. It opened in 1994 on a 10-year lease and was set to close at the end of July 2004, when the lease ran out.

name: L'Amie Donia
note: French bistro run by chef-owner Donia Bijan, opened in 1994 and rated Palo Alto's top restaurant by Zagat in 2004. It closed in early June 2004, and the new owner planned to reopen it as a French bistro called La Cheminee.

name: California Pizza Kitchen
note: Downtown branch of the California Pizza Kitchen chain, described in a 2005 review as 11 years old. It closed in mid-August 2014, while the chain's Stanford Shopping Center location stayed open.

name: Florentine Restaurant and Pasta Market
note: Northern Italian restaurant and fresh pasta market, part of a San Jose-based chain owned by the Del Monaco family. Palo Alto Weekly readers voted it Best Pasta in 1994 and 1996; the years shown are the earliest and latest sources found, and it likely operated longer.

name: The Artifactory
note: Craft shop and studio that held art workshops such as mask-making, listed in the Palo Alto Weekly in 1994. A craft shop on this block was forced out when a fire destroyed the one-story building at Hamilton and Emerson around 1996.

name: Pollo's Rotisserie Chicken
note: Rotisserie chicken restaurant that served chicken burritos, tacos and quesadillas. Palo Alto Weekly readers voted it best burrito in 1994; actual years open may be longer.

name: Nataraja
note: Indian restaurant known for mesquite grilling and Indian breads, listed at this address in the Palo Alto Weekly's 1994 restaurant guides, which called it a local institution. Its actual opening and closing years are unknown and were likely earlier and later.

name: Taxi's Hamburgers
note: Retro hamburger diner with booths, a counter and a jukebox at the corner of University and Waverley, part of a small Bay Area chain. Opened December 11, 1995; still open in 2008, closing year not yet confirmed.

name: Mango Cafe
note: Caribbean restaurant serving Trinidad and Tobago cuisine, which moved here in early 1995 after about five years on University Avenue. Palo Alto Weekly reviewed it in 1995 and 1998; when it closed has not been confirmed.

name: YogaSource
note: Heated Bikram yoga studio that opened in May 1995, said to be the first outside San Francisco to offer heated yoga. It moved to Hamilton Avenue in 2001.

name: The Adventures of Jerusha
note: Women's clothing store at 515 Cowper St selling colorful easy-care separates in natural fibers and custom-made outfits; featured in Palo Alto Weekly Shop Talk in June and December 1995. Years shown are the first and last years sources confirm it at this address.

name: Max's Eatz
note: Upscale deli offshoot of Max's Opera Cafe serving New York deli-style sandwiches, reviewed as new in April 1995. It closed within months, and World Wrapps was planned for the corner space by October 1995.

name: Noah's Bagels
note: New York-style bagel shop at the corner of University and Bryant, voted Palo Alto's best bagels in 1995 and for years after; the building that housed Noah's and Starbucks was slated for demolition in August 2008.

name: The Photographer's Gallery
note: Fine-art photography gallery that moved here from 732 Emerson St. in August 1995. Local exhibit listings place it at 536 Ramona St. through at least mid-2000.

name: Elbe Restaurant
note: German and Middle European restaurant that opened in 1995 in the former Rudyard's space at the top of University Avenue; Palo Alto's only German restaurant, it shared a kitchen with Rudy's Pub and closed in January 2010.

name: Mystic Cafe
note: Quirky multicultural restaurant opened in October 1995 by Theo's owner Michael Aroner in the same space, with live rhythm-and-blues guitar on Saturdays; listed at this address through September 1996, and Crescent Park Grill was there by 1997.

name: World Wrapps
note: Wrap and smoothie restaurant, a branch of a San Francisco chain, that was planned for the former Max's Eatz corner space in October 1995. It was listed here in a 1996 local food guide, but its exact opening and closing years are unknown.

name: Zibibbo
note: Pan-Mediterranean restaurant in a renovated yellow Victorian house spanning Kipling to Waverley; opened in 1997 and closed in April 2014 after a 17-year run, after which the space became offices.

name: Crescent Park Grill
note: Restaurant at 546 University Ave. with live jazz on Wednesday evenings in 1997; it had departed by July 2000, when Perry's opened in the space.

name: Zao Noodle Bar
note: Pan-Asian noodle bar that opened in spring 1997 and was reviewed by Metro that year. It had closed by 2011, when Oren's Hummus Shop opened in the space.

name: Antique Interiors West
note: Antique furnishings shop in the former Thompson's Bakery building, mentioned in the Palo Alto Weekly in 1998; actual years open may be longer.

name: Museum of American Heritage
note: A museum of American technology and everyday life, housed in the restored 1907 Williams House and garden. It opened to the public there in April 1998 and is still open.

name: Robaii Falafel
note: Family-run Persian restaurant at Hamilton Ave and Cowper St, in the former Penny Farthing space. Opened in May 1998 serving falafel, hummus, baba ghanoush and lamb pitas, and closed in April 2010 after 12 years; Siam Orchid later took the space.

name: Bella Luna
note: Italian restaurant (Bella Luna Ristorante Italiano), reviewed as newly opened by Metro Silicon Valley in 1999. It may have stayed open longer, but it closed before The Workshop opened at this address in 2011.

name: Lavanda Restaurant and Wine Bar
note: Mediterranean Italian restaurant and wine bar with a 600-bottle list that took over the former Good Earth space at the corner of University and Emerson in 2002. It closed in summer 2012 and was replaced by Campo 185.

name: Andalé Mexican Restaurant
note: Palo Alto branch of a Los Gatos-based Mexican restaurant, listed at this address by 2002 and remembered as a popular lunch spot. It had closed by 2015; the years shown are the earliest and latest sources found.

name: Vivre
note: Fitness and wellness studio on Emerson Street that offered yoga, cardio, Pilates, childcare and massage. It opened in May 2003 and closed around 2018; the street number is reported but not confirmed.

name: BayLeaf Cafe
note: Vegan cafe that took over the former Double Rainbow ice cream parlor space; reviewed in February 2003 and closed in October 2006.

name: Darshana Yoga
note: Yoga studio founded by Catherine De Los Santos. It opened on this block of High Street in July 2003 and ran until 2012, and it was featured in the Palo Alto Weekly's Best of 2006 yoga category.

name: Kiki's Candy
note: Popular downtown candy store that opened in 2003. Around 2005 it moved to Fabian Way in south Palo Alto because of rising rents and parking problems.

name: House of Bagels
note: A bagel shop on University Avenue that appeared in Palo Alto Weekly's Best Of winners lists. In late January 2015, after 27 years in business, its owner moved it to Edgewood Plaza on Embarcadero Road. Palo Alto Online's Peninsula Foodist reported it closing in 2015.

name: Patxi's Chicago Pizza
note: Chicago-style deep-dish pizzeria that opened in 2004 as the first restaurant of the Patxi's chain. Listings now show this location as closed, reportedly around 2022.

name: Stoa Restaurant & Wine Bar
note: Formerly vegetarian restaurant that moved downtown from a site near Highway 101 in late 2004, adding seafood and live jazz. It closed abruptly after Easter weekend in April 2005.

name: La Cheminée
note: French restaurant owned by Duane Hooton that opened in 2004 in the former L'Amie Donia space and was reviewed by Palo Alto Online that September. Later status unknown.

name: FORM Fitness
note: Downtown gym founded in 2003 on Forest Ave; won the city lease for the new building at 445 Bryant St in 2004 and moved there in 2005, operating for nearly two decades until it was evicted in 2022 after falling behind on rent.

name: Vino Locale
note: Wine bar and kitchen in a century-old house, opened in January 2005 by Randy Robinson and a partner. Still operating, with live music in its back garden. Palo Alto Online's Peninsula Foodist reported it opening in 2005.

name: The Parlor
note: Shop in the 1907 Thompson Bakery building, which for decades was the bakery's sales outlet. Its owners won a 2005 Palo Alto Stanford Heritage preservation award for restoring the building. Actual years open were likely longer.

name: Dragon Theatre
note: Small black-box theater with about 40 seats at the corner of Alma and Hamilton, run by Dragon Productions Theatre Company. It opened in February 2006 with The Heidi Chronicles and moved to a larger space in Redwood City in 2012.

name: California Yoga Center
note: Yoga studio with classes from beginner to advanced, listed at this address in local guides from 2006 and 2011. The studio later moved to Mountain View, and its years at this address may have been longer.

name: Lytton Gardens Health Care Center
note: Skilled nursing and rehabilitation facility with 145 licensed beds, run by Lytton Gardens, Inc. and listed here by 2006. State records now list it as Webster House, and it may be considerably older.

name: Sehbali Cafe and Hookah Shop
note: Cafe and hookah lounge in the brick Mills the Florist building at University Ave and Ramona St, billed as Palo Alto's first hookah business when it opened in late 2006. It served coffee, chai and light meals and has since closed; the closing year is not confirmed.

name: Lytton Roasting Company
note: Neighborhood coffee shop and roaster on the corner of Lytton, in business for many years before John's Cafe took over the space in 2012; some regulars remember it as the Palo Alto Roasting Company. Opening year not yet confirmed (open by 2007).

name: Kanpai Sushi
note: Family-owned Japanese restaurant serving sushi at 330 Lytton Ave since at least 2007, when it was named Palo Alto's best sushi spot; still operating there.

name: Spot A Pizza Place
note: Pizza restaurant that moved downtown around late 2008 after five years at Town & Country Village, taking over the former Espresso Bettola coffee house space. It closed abruptly in November 2017. Palo Alto Online's Peninsula Foodist reported it closing in 2018.

name: St. Michael's Alley
note: Long-running Palo Alto restaurant founded as a coffeehouse in 1959. After years at 806 Emerson St, the owners expanded into this larger dining space on Homer Ave in 2009; the 2011 Palo Alto Weekly Best Of lists the Homer Ave address for lunch and dinner, and the restaurant still operates there.

name: Uforia Studios

name: Sam's Chowder House
note: Downtown branch of the Half Moon Bay seafood restaurant. It opened in November 2013 in the former Campo 185 space and closed in December 2016, when the space was sold to Wahlburgers. Palo Alto Online's Peninsula Foodist reported it opening in 2013 and closing in 2017.

name: Webster House
